questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: wanted to go on an exchange in a country I had not visited before. In addition, it was important to me that it was an English-speaking country so I could communicate more easily with patients. I had also heard many positive things about exchange programs in Sydney, which played a significant role in my decision.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through Facebook, which worked well. I simply created a post and received many offers through that platform.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in a house with several other students from Denmark. It is important to find accommodation that is well connected in terms of public transport, and I also found it really nice to have roommates.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The academic supervisor at the hospital met us on the first day and gave us a tour of the hospital as well as the associated medical education center. Afterwards, we were assigned to the departments, where we were very well received.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was always the option to email or call the student advisory services to receive assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not have to choose classes myself; however, I was able to state my preferred hospital department, and they were very receptive to my wishes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You should ask any questions you have – everyone is very kind and helpful.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sydney got lots to offer and I would recommend exploring all areas in the city!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy - the aussies are very welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The students at the hospital were really kind, welcoming, and interested in learning about another culture. Just go up to them and ask – I only experienced positive responses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I experienced a genuine interest in getting to know new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Align your expectations with the department when you start, so you can get the most out of your placement.

2) Always speak up if there’s something you don’t understand or are unsure about – they are really good at teaching.

3) Dive in and take on patients yourself – they are often very kind and patient when you’re a foreign student.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can’t think of anything else for now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned a great deal about the healthcare system in a new country and how to interact with culturally diverse patients respectfully!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the biggest challenge at the beginning was figuring out how to express myself politely to patients from a different culture when giving difficult news or asking sensitive questions. However, I quickly learned this along the way and can take these experiences with me.
